feedback:
Pre-race review of the sensor spacing step from x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 to x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025, with sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 0.9 and line_loss last_direction unchanged. The best raced design is iteration 9 at 686.99. Iteration 7 to 8 showed that narrowing spacing from 0.02 to 0.015 steps moved slalom progress from 0.37 to 0.56, and the oval stayed at 20 of 20 with lower steering oscillation. Iteration 8 to 9 showed that base_speed 0.9 gave a small s-bend gain (finishes 17 to 18) and left slalom flat (0.56 to 0.53). Slalom is still 0 of 20 completions. Gain changes (iterations 5 and 6) did not move slalom, so the spacing trend is the strongest lever seen.

The candidate is valid: all positions are inside range, the weights are unchanged at (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), and sensor_size 0.016 is an allowed option. It is a moderate single-variable step (about 17 percent tighter than iteration 9). With fixed weights, the effective steering gain rises by roughly 1.2 times, so the main risks are a sharper steering response, more oval oscillation, and s-bend off-track ends. The candidate does not repeat the iteration 1 mistake of widening the array, and kp is held at 3.0 rather than raised. A further revision would cost two action runs and would add little beyond what the race will show. Racing it is the most informative next step, and the iteration 9 design remains the fallback.

How to read the race: (a) if slalom progress rises above 0.56 while the oval stays at 20 of 20 and s-bend finishes hold at 17 or more, keep this spacing and consider a final small base_speed or spacing refinement in the last iteration; (b) if s-bend finishes fall below 14 or the oval drops, return to the iteration 9 spacing (x = -0.03 to +0.03), which is the best raced base; (c) if slalom stays flat near 0.53 to 0.56, bend geometry is the limit, and the next test should be sensor_size or a single kd step, not more speed.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.56 with the oval at 20 of 20 and s-bend finishes at 14 or more, keep geometry.sensor_positions at x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025, and in the final iteration consider controller.base_speed 0.8 only if s-bend completion_time stays comfortably under 3.0 s (iteration 9 mean 2.37 s at 0.9).

If s-bend finishes fall below 14 of 20 or the oval drops below 20 of 20, return geometry.sensor_positions to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 with sensor_size 0.016, kp 3.0, kd 0.8, base_speed 0.9, because iteration 9 (686.99) is the base to beat.

If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.3 (iteration 9 was 0.13) with the tighter array, reduce controller.kp from 3.0 to about 2.7 rather than widening or narrowing spacing again, since the tighter array raises effective gain by about 1.2 times with fixed weights.
